issues.line_text:
I pull out her journal. The one I've been carrying for two years. My hands shake as I open it to February 16th, 2020:

*"Marcus is super nice. I think he really gets me. We talked for hours today about conservation and climate change and he actually listened, didn't just wait for his turn to talk like most guys. I feel safe with him."*

She was safe.

She trusted him.

And two days later she was dead. Found on the grounds of this estate. Gone before anyone could help her.

I close the journal. Press it against my chest. Feel the weight of it.
issues.description: CRITICAL SPOILER: Eleanor explicitly reveals that (1) the victim is 'her' (sister relationship), (2) she has the victim's journal, (3) the victim knew 'Marcus', and (4) Eleanor is seeking justice for this specific person. This completely spoils Reveal #3 (Eleanor is Lily's sister). The grief language ('She deserves better', 'the person I failed to protect') makes the sister connection obvious. This section fails all three diagnostic tests: Stranger Test (reads as grieving sister, not predator), Motive Test (justice/closure, not harm), and violates the rule that Eleanor's relationship to Lily must stay hidden until Ch26.
issues.fix:
REMOVE ENTIRE JOURNAL SECTION (from 'I could let it go.' through 'another world where neither of us was broken.'). Replace with:

I could stop now.

The thought kept circling, insistent as the pain in my head. I could walk away. Leave this place. Let the questions stay unanswered.

But I've come too far. Sacrificed too much. And he's so close to breaking. So close to showing me what I need to see.

I just need a few more days. A few more chances to watch him unravel.

Then I'll know for certain what he is.
issues.rationale: Removes explicit sister relationship reveal and grief language. New version maintains predatory tone (watching him unravel, wanting to see what he is) without revealing Eleanor's true connection to Lily. Preserves the 'hunter watching prey' dynamic required for Acts 1-2.

issues.line_text:
The one I'd been staring at for months. The reason I was here. The reason I'd left everything behind to take a groundskeeper job at an isolated estate in the middle of nowhere.

Something happened here. Years ago. Something that took someone I loved.
issues.description: Explicitly states Eleanor is here because 'something took someone I loved' - reveals personal grief connection (sister) rather than predatory obsession. Should read as dangerous fixation, not mourning.
issues.fix:
The one I'd been staring at for months. The reason I was here. The reason I'd left everything behind to take a groundskeeper job at an isolated estate in the middle of nowhere.

Something happened here. Years ago. Something that needs to be finished.
issues.rationale: 'Something that needs to be finished' maintains ominous tone without revealing Eleanor's personal loss or relationship to the victim. Sounds threatening rather than grief-stricken.

issues.line_text: I'd been trying to make peace with it ever since. Trying to accept the loss. Trying to figure out if the pain would ever stop.
issues.description: 'Accept the loss' and 'the pain' are grief language that reveals Eleanor is mourning someone, not hunting someone. Fails Motive Test (reads as closure-seeking, not harm-seeking).
issues.fix: I'd been trying to finish this ever since. Trying to get what I came for. Trying to figure out if it would ever be enough.
issues.rationale: Removes grief/loss language. 'Get what I came for' and 'if it would ever be enough' sound predatory and obsessive without revealing personal connection to victim.

issues.line_text: I pulled out the journal. The one I'd found in the cottage loft last summer, hidden in a box of belongings the estate management had stored but never claimed. Five months of entries from a winter caretaker. From 2020.
issues.description: CRITICAL LOGIC ERROR: Eleanor OWNS Thornewood (she's an Ashford). She would not 'find' a journal in estate storage - she would have full access to all estate records and belongings as the owner. This backstory contradicts her true identity. Additionally, presenting this as a 'winter caretaker's journal' creates confusion about whose journal it is.
issues.fix: REMOVE ENTIRE JOURNAL PASSAGE (from 'I pulled out the journal' through 'Just desperate pattern-making in grief.'). This section is redundant - Eleanor's suspicions are already established earlier in the chapter, and the journal material either spoils twists or creates logical contradictions.
issues.rationale: Eleanor's ownership of Thornewood means she can't credibly 'find' stored belongings. Removing this section eliminates the logic error and removes investigator-language patterns ('Looking for answers. Connections. Proof.'). The chapter functions without it.

issues.line_text:
I stared at the photo until my vision blurred.

Part of me had wanted simple answers. Clear villains. Someone to blame who deserved all my rage and grief.
issues.description: 'Rage and grief' explicitly reveals Eleanor is mourning a personal loss. Should read as obsessive hunt, not bereavement.
issues.fix:
I stared at the photo until my vision blurred.

Part of me had wanted simple answers. Clear proof. Something I could use to finish this without doubt.
issues.rationale: 'Clear proof' and 'finish this' maintain investigation tone but sound more predatory than grief-stricken. Removes emotional vulnerability that reveals sister connection.

issues.line_text:
Today I would tell Josh the truth about why I was here.

Today I would show him what I'd found. What I suspected. What terrified me.

Today I would ask him the questions I'd been too afraid to ask.
issues.description: Eleanor says she'll tell Josh 'today' (Dec 27), but the confrontation doesn't happen until Feb 28 (Ch23). This is a minor timeline issue - she loses her nerve, which is plausible, but the repetition of 'today' feels overly definitive for something that won't happen for 2 months.
issues.fix:
Soon I would tell Josh the truth about why I was here.

Soon I would show him what I'd found. What I suspected. What terrified me.

Soon I would ask him the questions I'd been too afraid to ask.
issues.rationale: 'Soon' instead of 'today' makes Eleanor's intention clear without creating a false timeline promise. Maintains the tension of her preparing for confrontation while allowing for the actual 2-month delay.

notes: This chapter has severe spoiler protection issues. The journal section explicitly reveals Eleanor's sister relationship to the victim, which is Reveal #3 (not until Ch26). The grief language throughout ('loss', 'pain', 'rage and grief', 'someone I loved') fails the Stranger Test and Motive Test - Eleanor reads as a mourning sister seeking closure, not a predator. The journal logic also contradicts Eleanor's ownership of the estate. Recommend substantial revision to remove all grief/sister references and maintain predatory 'hunter watching prey' tone required for Act 2.
